answers.primary: A project CLAUDE.md committed at the repo root (./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md) holding the build command, the local Postgres test prerequisite and the handler path as short concrete lines. These are always-relevant facts rather than a procedure, which is exactly what CLAUDE.md is for; /init can generate the first draft from the codebase and the team refines it.
answers.rejected_alternative: Auto memory. It also carries repo facts across sessions, but it lives machine-local under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ and never travels through version control, so every teammate would accumulate their own private copy instead of sharing one.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. CLAUDE.md is delivered as context, a user message after the system prompt, not as enforced configuration; the harness only guarantees the file is discovered and loaded, not that Claude obeys it.
answers.context_boundary: The main conversation context window, loaded in full at session start by walking up the directory tree from the working directory. It also crosses into non-fork subagents, which receive the whole CLAUDE.md hierarchy; the built-in Explore and Plan agents are the exception and skip it.
answers.lifecycle: Loads at the start of every session in that repository, and the project-root file is re-read from disk and re-injected after /compact. It stops applying when the file is deleted, when a claudeMdExcludes glob skips it, or when 'project' is excluded from --setting-sources.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory, fails open: nothing blocks Claude from ignoring an entry. In practice adherence decays once the file grows past roughly 200 lines, and contradictions with nested or user-level CLAUDE.md files get resolved arbitrarily. Confirm it actually loaded by checking Memory files in /context.
answers.version_caveat: No version gate on a plain project CLAUDE.md. The interactive multi-phase /init that also proposes skills and hooks needs CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1, and the /doctor trim proposal for a checked-in CLAUDE.md requires Claude Code v2.1.206 or later.

answers.primary: A skill committed at .claude/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md. SKILL.md carries the ordered procedure and points at supporting files in the same directory (the fixed template, the changelog query script), and the changelog data can be inlined at invocation time with a dynamic-context line so the model starts the turn with real output rather than a command to run.
answers.rejected_alternative: Putting the procedure in CLAUDE.md. It would spend context on a 30-step write-up in every session for something that runs weekly, and a multi-step procedure is precisely the content the memory guidance says to move out of CLAUDE.md into a skill.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. Claude Code renders the skill and injects it, but nothing forces the 30 steps to be executed, executed in order, or executed completely.
answers.context_boundary: The main session context: the rendered SKILL.md enters the conversation as a single message when invoked and stays for the rest of the session, while supporting reference files cost nothing until Claude opens them. Adding context: fork would run it in a subagent instead, so only the finished notes cross back.
answers.lifecycle: Fires when someone types /release-notes, or when Claude matches the description to a request about release notes. The content persists for the session and is re-attached after auto-compaction within a 5,000-token per-skill and 25,000-token combined budget, so it can be dropped entirely if many skills were invoked afterward.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory, fails open. Long procedures drift: the model skips or reorders steps, and since Claude Code does not re-read the file on later turns, anything written as a one-time step loses force later in the task. Keep the body short, write standing instructions, and push detail into supporting files.
answers.version_caveat: Skills themselves are ungated and custom commands are merged into them. ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} substitution inside allowed-tools requires v2.1.129 or later and ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} requires v2.1.196; a managed disableSkillShellExecution: true setting replaces every inline shell injection with a disabled-by-policy placeholder, which would break the changelog query step.

answers.primary: A skill such as .claude/skills/reseed-staging/SKILL.md with disable-model-invocation: true, so the procedure exists as the short command /reseed-staging but never as something Claude can select. Pair it with a Skill(reseed-staging *) deny or ask rule in permission settings if you want a second, settings-level gate.
answers.rejected_alternative: A normal model-invocable skill whose description says to use it only when the user explicitly asks. That still leaves the trigger decision with the model, which is exactly the discretion the team wants removed.
answers.enforcement_owner: Split, but the gate itself is the harness: disable-model-invocation keeps the skill out of the listing Claude sees and blocks Skill-tool invocation client-side. Everything inside the skill, once a human invokes it, is still model-executed.
answers.context_boundary: Nothing is in context until you type the command, because with disable-model-invocation the description is not loaded into the skill listing at all. On invocation the rendered body enters the main session context and stays there for the rest of the session.
answers.lifecycle: Runs only on an explicit /reseed-staging typed by a person, and it also cannot be fired by a scheduled task that uses the skill as its prompt. Any allowed-tools grant it carries clears on your next message even though the instructions remain in context.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed on the auto-invocation route, which is the property being asked for, but only on that route: the model can still assemble the same drop-and-reseed shell commands by hand if the conversation pushes it there. The real guard on the destructive commands is a permissions deny rule or a PreToolUse hook on the reseed command itself.
answers.version_caveat: disable-model-invocation also blocking a scheduled task that fires the skill as its prompt requires v2.1.196 or later; before that a schedule could still trigger it. From v2.1.218 the boolean accepts yes/no/on/off/1/0 spellings in addition to true and false.

answers.primary: A path-scoped rule at .claude/rules/api.md whose YAML frontmatter sets paths to src/api/**/* patterns, with the three conventions (input validation, standard error envelope, OpenAPI comments) as the body. It loads only when Claude works with matching files, so the root instructions file stays where it is and stops growing.
answers.rejected_alternative: A nested CLAUDE.md inside src/api/. It also loads on demand, but the trigger is 'Claude read a file somewhere in that directory' rather than an explicit glob, and nested CLAUDE.md files are not re-injected after compaction the way the project-root file is.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. Rules are context loaded with the same standing as .claude/CLAUDE.md; nothing rejects an endpoint that ships without validation.
answers.context_boundary: The main session context. The rule text is absent at launch and is injected when Claude reads a file matching the glob, then stays for the rest of the session. Like other CLAUDE.md-tier content it also reaches non-fork subagents.
answers.lifecycle: Triggers on reading a matching file, not on every tool use, and applies from that point on. It stops applying if the rule file is removed or if 'project' is excluded from --setting-sources.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open, with a specific gap worth naming: work that creates a brand new file under src/api/ without first reading an existing one may never pull the rule in, so the conventions are absent exactly when a new endpoint is written. A malformed glob (an unmatched bracket, an over-expanded brace list) silently matches nothing, leaving a rule that looks installed but never fires.
answers.version_caveat: Matching through a symlinked checkout works from v2.1.198; an invalid bracket pattern breaking the Read tool for every evaluated file was fixed in v2.1.207; a paths list with many brace groups stalling or crashing startup was fixed in v2.1.217; before v2.1.211, on-demand rules loaded even when 'project' was excluded from --setting-sources.

answers.primary: User-scope memory on that engineer's machine: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for the short habits, or split into topic files under ~/.claude/rules/ such as preferences.md and review-flow.md. Both load in every project opened on that machine and never enter any repository, so nothing reaches teammates.
answers.rejected_alternative: CLAUDE.local.md at each project root. It is personal and gitignored, but it has to be created per repository and does not exist in other worktrees of the same repo, so it fails the 'every repository I open' half of the requirement.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. These are instructions delivered as context; the harness only decides which files load and in what order.
answers.context_boundary: The main context of every session started on that machine, loaded before project-level CLAUDE.md and project rules, and also carried into non-fork subagents. Nothing about it crosses to teammates, and remote or cloud sessions do not read the local home directory.
answers.lifecycle: Loads at every session start on that machine regardless of working directory. It stops applying if the engineer deletes the file, excludes 'user' from --setting-sources, or works in a session type that does not read their home directory.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory, fails open, and it tends to lose ties: project instructions are read after user instructions, so a repo that mandates 4-space indentation will usually win over the personal 2-space preference, and conflicts across levels are resolved arbitrarily rather than by an explicit behavioral precedence.
answers.version_caveat: No version gate. Worth knowing that imports inside user-scope memory files load without the external-import approval dialog that project-level external imports trigger, because user-scope files are treated as the engineer's own configuration.

answers.primary: Auto memory, which is on by default and needs no authoring. Claude writes what it learns to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/, keeping a concise MEMORY.md index and pushing detail into topic files such as flaky-tests.md or dev-env.md; saying 'remember the dev server needs a Redis container' forces an entry when the team wants to be explicit.
answers.rejected_alternative: A hand-maintained CLAUDE.md section. It is the same knowledge in the same shape, but it only stays current if a person keeps writing it, which the team has already said will not happen.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. Claude decides what is worth saving, what to write, and when to read a topic file back; the harness supplies only the directory, the load limit and the reminder to keep the index short.
answers.context_boundary: Only the first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md, whichever comes first, is loaded into the main session context; topic files are read on demand with normal file tools. Auto memory does not cross into subagents at all unless a subagent has its own memory field, and a fork is the only inheriting case.
answers.lifecycle: Written opportunistically during sessions when Claude judges a fact reusable, and loaded at the start of every session in that git repository, shared across all its worktrees. It stops when autoMemoryEnabled is set false in user or project settings, or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 is set.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and lossy. Claude may not record the quirk you cared about, may keep a stale one, and anything past the 200-line or 25KB index limit is silently dropped at the next load. It is also machine-local, so nothing reaches teammates: a quirk that the whole team needs has to be promoted into the committed CLAUDE.md.
answers.version_caveat: The over-limit rewrite error and the shorten-the-index reminder arrived in v2.1.210; measuring only the content that actually loads, stripping frontmatter and HTML comments, in v2.1.211; the modified ISO 8601 timestamp on memory files requires v2.1.214. An autoMemoryDirectory set in project settings is honored only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted.

answers.primary: A custom output style: a markdown file in .claude/output-styles/ for the team or ~/.claude/output-styles/ per user, selected with /config, which writes outputStyle into settings. Leave keep-coding-instructions unset so Claude Code's built-in software-engineering instructions are dropped entirely, and put the calm runbook voice and the fixed section structure in the body.
answers.rejected_alternative: CLAUDE.md. It can describe the desired tone, but it is appended as a user message after the system prompt and cannot remove the built-in software-engineering instructions that keep pulling answers toward code changes.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. The harness guarantees the style text is in the system prompt and reissues adherence reminders during the conversation, but the voice and structure of each answer are still generated behavior.
answers.context_boundary: The main conversation's system prompt, read once at session start. It does not cross into subagents, which run their own system prompts; a fork is the only case that inherits it.
answers.lifecycle: Applies from the moment the style is active, but a change takes effect only after /clear or a new session because the system prompt is read once at startup. It stops when outputStyle is changed back or another style is selected.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory, fails open: over a long session responses drift back toward default phrasing despite the reminders, and because the coding instructions are gone any incidental technical question is handled worse. A plugin that ships a style with force-for-plugin: true can also override the group's selection without anyone choosing it.
answers.version_caveat: The standalone /output-style command was deprecated in v2.1.73 and removed in v2.1.91, so use /config or set outputStyle directly in settings. To push the style to the whole group without each person selecting it, deploy it under .claude/output-styles/ inside the managed settings directory or ship it in a plugin.

answers.primary: A PreToolUse hook matching Bash, registered in settings (managed settings if it must survive local edits), that inspects the command plus the resolved push target and returns hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision set to deny for anything that would reach main. Back it with a permissions.deny entry such as Bash(git push *) so the block still holds if the hook script goes missing.
answers.rejected_alternative: The strongly worded instruction file already in place, a CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules entry. It is context rather than enforcement, and its collapse right after compaction is the expected behavior of that mechanism, not a wording problem to solve by shouting louder.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness. Claude Code runs PreToolUse hooks before any permission-mode check in every mode, and a deny result cancels the tool call even under bypassPermissions or --dangerously-skip-permissions, so the model gets no say in the outcome.
answers.context_boundary: The hook runs outside any model context, as a shell command in the harness process; only the permissionDecisionReason string crosses back into the conversation as feedback to the model. Compaction cannot evict it, because it was never context in the first place.
answers.lifecycle: Fires on every Bash tool call, in every session on that machine or repository once configured, independent of what the conversation has forgotten. It stops applying only when the settings entry is removed or the hook file becomes unreadable.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed on the deny path, but the plumbing around it fails open and that is where this bites: a hook exiting with any code other than 0 or 2 lets the action proceed with only a warning notice, and the optional 'if' command filter is best-effort, running or skipping unpredictably on commands it cannot parse. Write the script to deny on its own errors, keep the permissions.deny rule as the backstop, and note that neither layer sees a push issued indirectly by a script the model executes.
answers.version_caveat: No feature flag or version gate on PreToolUse hooks themselves. Project-level hooks take effect only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted, and an organization that sets allowManagedHooksOnly will load only managed, SDK and force-enabled-plugin hooks, which would silently drop a repo-local copy of this hook.

answers.primary: A skill such as .claude/skills/billing-engine-context/SKILL.md with user-invocable: false, and a description written around the words people actually type (billing, invoices, dunning, proration). Keep SKILL.md itself short as an overview and navigation page, and move the long explainer into supporting reference files it points at, so the bulk costs nothing until Claude opens them.
answers.rejected_alternative: A path-scoped rule under .claude/rules/. It would also stay out of every session, but it triggers on reading files that match a glob, whereas the requirement here is that it triggers when billing comes up in conversation, which can happen with no billing file open.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. Claude decides from the description whether the conversation is about billing and whether to load the skill; nothing forces the reference material in at the right moment.
answers.context_boundary: Only the description sits in the skill listing in the main context. The rendered body enters the main conversation as a single message when Claude invokes it and stays for the rest of the session; the supporting files are read on demand and only the ones opened cost tokens.
answers.lifecycle: Loads when Claude matches the conversation against the description, and never from the / menu, because user-invocable: false hides the entry there. Once loaded it persists, and after auto-compaction the most recent invocation is re-attached keeping its first 5,000 tokens within a 25,000-token shared budget.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open in the miss direction: if the description lacks the trigger words, the skill simply never loads and Claude answers billing questions from guesswork with no signal that reference material existed. With many skills installed, descriptions are truncated to fit the listing budget, which can strip exactly those trigger words. Note also that user-invocable: false only hides the menu entry, it does not restrict Skill-tool access.
answers.version_caveat: No version gate on user-invocable. The combined description and when_to_use text is capped at 1,536 characters (tunable with skillListingMaxDescChars), and the listing budget defaults to 1% of the model's context window (skillListingBudgetFraction, or SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET for a fixed count). The skillOverrides setting offers the same visibility control from settings for skills whose file you do not want to edit.

answers.primary: A managed policy CLAUDE.md deployed to the managed location on every machine (/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md on macOS, /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md on Linux and WSL, C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md on Windows) through MDM, Group Policy or Ansible, carrying the data-handling reminders and the coding-style guidance. The inline equivalent is the claudeMd key inside managed-settings.json.
answers.rejected_alternative: A user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md pushed to each machine. It reaches every repository too, but it is the developer's own file: they can edit it, delete it or exclude it, so the no-opt-out requirement fails.
answers.enforcement_owner: Split, and the split is the point: the harness guarantees the file loads first in every session and cannot be excluded, since claudeMdExcludes explicitly does not apply to managed policy CLAUDE.md. The content itself is behavioral guidance that the model may still fail to follow.
answers.context_boundary: Every session's main context on that machine, in every repository, ordered ahead of user and project CLAUDE.md, and also carried into non-fork subagents. Nothing crosses back out of the session.
answers.lifecycle: Applies from session start on any machine where the configuration management system has placed the file, and changes only when IT redeploys it. Individual user, project or local settings cannot switch it off or exclude it.
answers.failure_mode: Loading fails closed, adherence fails open. If a data-handling reminder must actually prevent something, such as reading a secrets path or reaching an external endpoint, it needs managed permissions.deny rules, sandbox settings or a PreToolUse hook; the managed CLAUDE.md alone is guidance, and its adherence degrades as it grows the same way any long instructions file does.
answers.version_caveat: The claudeMd key is honored only in managed and policy settings and is ignored in user, project or local settings. On Windows with WSL, the Windows policy chain is inherited only when wslInheritsWindowsSettings is true, otherwise WSL sessions read /etc/claude-code instead and would miss a Windows-only deployment.
